en.intro: Krishna describes the heaven-world as a vast reward that ends. Listen for the moment when the soul must return to the mortal world.
en.notice: Heaven bought with merit runs out, Krishna says, and the buyer comes back down to earth.
en.next: He then turns to those who fix their minds on him alone, offering a different kind of security.
en.meaning: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going.

hi.intro: कृष्ण स्वर्गलोक को एक विशाल इनाम बताते हैं जो समाप्त हो जाता है। सुनिए उस पल को जब आत्मा को वापस मृत्युलोक में लौटना पड़ता है।
hi.meaning: वे उस विशाल स्वर्गलोकके भोगोंको भोगकर पुण्य क्षीण होनेपर मृत्युलोकमें आ जाते हैं ।  इस प्रकार तीनों वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम धर्मका आश्रय लिये हुए भोगोंकी कामना करनेवाले मनुष्य आवागमनको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
hi.notice: यहाँ पुण्य एक बैलेंस है जो खत्म हो जाता है और फिर व्यक्ति को वापस धरती पर लौटना पड़ता है।
hi.next: फिर वे उन लोगों की ओर मुड़ते हैं जो केवल उन्हीं का ध्यान करते हैं, और एक अलग तरह की सुरक्षा का वचन देते हैं।

borrowed: "Listen to the pair क्षीणे पुण्ये, merit having become exhausted. It is a bank balance that runs out, and then the person must return to the mortal world." (The phrase 'bank balance' is not in the SOURCE. However, this is a metaphorical explanation and not a factual claim about the text. The actual borrowed content is in the intro, which states 'showing that even heaven is a temporary stop' and 'reason the soul must come back down', which is the content of the NEXT verse (verse 22) about Krishna offering a different kind of security and carrying their welfare. The intro for verse 21 should only focus on the temporary nature of heaven from this verse, not the transition to verse 22.)
